Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just keep it to the accident, if that's alright.
Q: That's fine. We'll keep identifying details to a minimum for this file. Can you describe where the collision
happened?
A: It was in a shopping center parking lot in Katy, Texas. I was pulling out of a space near the main entrance, going
slowly, maybe five miles an hour.
Q: What happened next?
A: A car came down the aisle from my right side. I didn't see it until its front bumper was already across my passenger
door. I hit the brake, but there wasn't time to avoid it.
Q: Were you wearing a seatbelt?
A: Yes, I was. The belt locked up hard when I stopped, and that's when my right sohulder jerked forward.
Q: Did you feel any pain right away?
A: Not much at first. About twenty minutes later, my shoulder started aching, and by evening I couldn't lift my arm
above my chest without a sharp pain.
Q: Did you seek medical attention?
A: Yes. I went to an urgent care clinic the next morning. They took X-rays and told me to rest it and follow up with my
own doctor.
Q: Have you had any previous injuries or treatment to that shoulder?
A: No, nothing I can recall. I've had no problems with it before.
Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm still having trouble sleeping on that side. I'd like to get this resolved so I can get back to physical
therapy.
Q: Understood. This concludes the recorded statement. Thank you.
</page>

it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
